# Introduction

{{< lipsum 1 >}}

This guide also includes a sample `.bib` file of some of my publications because I want to show you how to cite things. You can do this automatically with `BibTeX` underneath the hood. Watch this, and figure out how to make this work for your case by observing the arguments in the YAML and investing in a citation management software. I strongly recommend `JabRef`, no matter how quaint its GUI is.[^jabref] I've published a few things in the past, a lot with my adviser. These include @millergibler2011dtnc, @gibleretal2012iia, @giblermiller2012cfap, @giblermiller2013qv, @giblermiller2014etts, and  @gibleretal2016amid (among others). Cite my solo stuff too. These citations include @miller2013tdpi, @miller2017ieea, @miller2017etst, and @miller2018etttc. These are just a few to get started.[^more]

[^jabref]: I've used `JabRef` for almost 20 years and it gets the job done. Those that are aware of citation management software often invest in Zotero. I'm sure it's fine, but export whatever you have in Zotero to a `.bib` file. That's what you need for this to work. Hey, would you look at that. Notice how you can generate a footnote!

[^more]: I have more things of mine you can cite.

# Second Section of Your Paper

{{< lipsum 2-3 >}}

Students, notice how you can reference this specific table with @tbl-cars in the Quarto document. I would strongly advise the use of some other table-rendering package for Quarto/R Markdown, like `{tinytable}` or `{kableExtra}`.[^user] This, however, does the job and doesn't require additional package dependencies.

[^user]: I am assuming my students are using the R programming language because that is the programming language I teach them. 

```{r}
#| tbl-cap: A Summary Table of the `cars` Data Set in Base R
#| label: tbl-cars
knitr::kable(summary(cars))
```
